label: Early original-phase steps (t=1-4) after a prefix dominated by s/l/v/y/w
explanation: Fires almost only in the original input phase (99.9% of mass), at t=1-4, peaking at t=2 (58% of mass). It never fires at t=0, the delimiter, or in the copy phase. It needs a prefix made up mostly of the letters s, l, v, y, w (prev_tok, prev2_tok and first_tok lift of 3-7x); the predicate asks for at least one of these with at most one other token earlier. The largest activations come after repeated s/l (e.g. s s then 0) and also depend on the current token: 0, q, g, z, s, i, l, b push it up. The current-token effect is graded, not a clean gate: adding it as a condition cut recall to about 0.55. The predicate covers about 94% of mass but precision is low (about 0.2), because many prefixes that fit the rule stay below threshold, so the neuron seems to sum letter-identity contributions rather than act as a crisp detector. It weakens with more digits among the original tokens and is mostly silent on repeated tokens (in_first=0).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=s (+5.50), prev_tok=<DEL> (+5.36), prev_tok=y (+5.09), prev_tok=v (+5.03), prev_tok=l (+4.60), prev_tok=w (+3.98). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-7.66), prev3_tok=p (-4.07), orig1=f (-4.06), in_tok=k (-3.95).
